title: Surgical prophylactic drainage in robotic-assisted complex hepatectomy
summary: After liver surgery, drains are often routinely placed to detect and remove intraabdominal fluid collections such as blood or bile at an early stage. However, recent studies suggest that these drains may also cause disadvantages, including infections, pain, delayed recovery, and longer hospital stays. While drains are increasingly omitted in minimally invasive procedures, they are still commonly used in more complex operations. The SPLASH trial therefore investigates whether avoiding drains can reduce complications after complex robotic liver surgery.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: No prophylactic use of perihepatic abdominal drainage after complex robotic hepatectomy
Prophylactic use of perihepatic abdominal drainage after complex robotic hepatectomy

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Elective complex robotic hepatectomies for benign or malignant lesions 
- Age equal to or greater than 18 years
- ASA I-III
- Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- pregnancy and breastfeeding
- vascular reconstruction and/or extrahepatic resections
- Impaired mental state or language barrier
- Suspected lack of compliance
